title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #7

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An orphan is (1 mark)
   A. a woman whose husband has died
   B. a person who looks after children
   C. a child whose parents have both died
   D. a brother or a sister

2. Which word has the same first sound as 'tie'? (1 mark)
   A. die
   B. fan
   C. two
   D. van

3. A word has two meanings in the dictionary. What should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore both
   B. Use the first meaning always
   C. Use the last meaning always
   D. Choose the meaning that fits your sentence

4. Which is written in block letters? (1 mark)
   A. WANJIKU KAMAU, in capital letters only
   B. Wanjiku Kamau, with capitals at the start of each name
   C. Wanjiku, in joined writing
   D. wanjiku kamau, in small letters

5. Which information is a school detail? (1 mark)
   A. Your date of birth
   B. Name of the head teacher
   C. Your favourite food
   D. Your weight

6. Target sounds: Which word has the sound /ɔɪ/? (1 mark)
   A. kite
   B. enjoy
   C. car
   D. bird

7. A direct question is one whose answer (1 mark)
   A. has no words
   B. is written in the text
   C. is a joke
   D. is not in the text

8. Which question is indirect? (1 mark)
   A. Where did she cry?
   B. Who cried?
   C. Why do you think the girl cried?
   D. When did the girl cry?

9. An inferential question needs you to (1 mark)
   A. guess without reading
   B. copy a sentence
   C. use clues and think
   D. skip the text

10. Which sentence uses 'a lot of' correctly? (1 mark)
   A. There are a lot of children in the yard.
   B. There are lot of children in the yard.
   C. There are alot of children in the yard.
   D. There are a lot children in the yard.

11. Which of these words is written with a double consonant in the middle? (1 mark)
   A. play
   B. stop
   C. dinner
   D. drink

12. In the word 'emergency', which syllable is stressed? (1 mark)
   A. The fourth
   B. The first
   C. The second
   D. The third

13. In which direction does the sun rise? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. North
   C. East
   D. South

14. Which pronoun replaces 'the children'? (1 mark)
   A. it
   B. they
   C. she
   D. he

15. 'She would like to be ___.' Which fits? (1 mark)
   A. to farm
   B. a farmer
   C. farmed
   D. farming

16. Independent reading means (1 mark)
   A. reading aloud to the class only
   B. reading only for exams
   C. reading on your own without being told what to read
   D. copying sentences

17. What is the superlative form of 'big'? (1 mark)
   A. biger
   B. bigest
   C. biggest
   D. more big

18. What is the comparative of 'happy'? (1 mark)
   A. happiest
   B. happyer
   C. happier
   D. more happy

19. Why is it important to plan a composition? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the story longer without ideas
   B. It hides your ideas
   C. It stops you from writing
   D. It keeps the ideas in order

20. The inbox is where (1 mark)
   A. deleted files are burnt
   B. messages you receive are kept
   C. the keyboard is stored
   D. messages waiting to be sent are kept

21. A pictorial composition is (1 mark)
   A. a song
   B. a story written from a set of pictures
   C. a map
   D. a shopping list

22. Pictures and stories: Which sentence describes a feeling? (1 mark)
   A. The message travelled.
   B. She was very happy to hear from him.
   C. He clicked Send.
   D. The computer was on.

23. Which sentence talks about a finished action in the past? (1 mark)
   A. Kamau is buying data bundles now.
   B. Kamau bought data bundles yesterday.
   C. Kamau buys data bundles every week.
   D. Kamau will buy data bundles tomorrow.

24. Which helping verb completes: 'They ____ watching TV when the power went off.'? (1 mark)
   A. were
   B. is
   C. was
   D. am

25. Which word begins with the sound /ʧ/? (1 mark)
   A. sack
   B. chicken
   C. sun
   D. soil

26. How long should the narrative composition be at this level? (1 mark)
   A. About 500 words
   B. About 60 to 80 words
   C. About 10 words
   D. About 300 words

27. Which word means 'to move from one person or place to another' (for example an illness)? (1 mark)
   A. signs
   B. cure
   C. spread
   D. diet

28. In which word does the letter s say /z/? (1 mark)
   A. class
   B. sun
   C. sit
   D. easy

29. Which word is an adverb of manner? (1 mark)
   A. never
   B. outside
   C. tomorrow
   D. carefully

30. Which adverb has the same form as its adjective? (1 mark)
   A. gently
   B. quickly
   C. slowly
   D. hard

31. Which end mark is right for: 'How many books have you read'? (1 mark)
   A. .
   B. ?
   C. !
   D. ,

32. Which of these is a coordinating conjunction? (1 mark)
   A. tidy
   B. quickly
   C. but
   D. broom

33. Which sentence uses the sense of smell? (1 mark)
   A. The towel is rough.
   B. The soap gives off a fresh smell.
   C. The tap drips.
   D. The wall is white.

34. Which is an example of a nonverbal cue? (1 mark)
   A. A word
   B. A song
   C. A sentence
   D. A thumbs-up

35. Which is a fact that can be checked? (1 mark)
   A. Netball is boring.
   B. A netball team has seven players.
   C. Everyone should play netball.
   D. Netball is the nicest game.

36. What does 'A stitch in time saves nine' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Time is money
   B. Nine stitches are better than one
   C. Fixing a small problem early prevents a bigger one
   D. Sewing is always fun

37. Which sentence is in the present perfect? (1 mark)
   A. She will finish.
   B. She has finished.
   C. She was finishing.
   D. She finishes.

38. What is a byline? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. The price of the paper
   C. The name of the writer of an article
   D. An advert

39. Which preposition means 'facing'? (1 mark)
   A. among
   B. between
   C. behind
   D. opposite

40. What is the -ing form of 'run'? (1 mark)
   A. runing
   B. runeing
   C. runnning
   D. running

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write one sentence with 'enough ... to' and one with 'a lot of' about your school. (3 marks)

42. Rewrite in the plural: 'The child put a loaf and a tomato in the box.' (3 marks)

43. Explain the difference between skimming and scanning. (2 marks)

44. Write the comparative and superlative of: happy, beautiful. (2 marks)

45. Rewrite with correct capital letters and full stops: 'we visited lake victoria in august' (3 marks)

46. Write a short dialogue of four lines between two learners about sending an email. (4 marks)

47. Write four sentences using in, on, under and between. (4 marks)

48. Write two words that contain /ɛə/, two that begin with /j/ and one that has /ʒ/. (5 marks)

49. Complete the simile and explain it: 'as cold as ______'. (2 marks)

50. Tell in three sentences how to set up a reading club. (3 marks)

51. Write two similes to describe a tractor and a hot day. (2 marks)

52. Write the past participle of: write, see, take. (3 marks)

53. Write two words with the sound /uː/ and two words with /ʊ/. (2 marks)

54. Write two words with the sound /aɪ/ and use one in a sentence. (2 marks)

55. Explain the difference in meaning between 'hopping' and 'hoping'. Use each in a sentence. (3 marks)

56. List three steps to follow before writing a pictorial composition. (3 marks)

57. Write four sentences for a short speech about your favourite game. (4 marks)

58. Write the minimal pairs for: ship, seat, sock. (3 marks)

59. From the passage about Mama Neema, what can you tell about her character? Give a reason. (3 marks)

60. Correct these sentences: (a) 'I have money enough to buy bread.' (b) 'She has alot of friends.' (2 marks)

61. Explain how /v/ and /w/ are made differently. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — a child whose parents have both died
   An orphan has lost both parents.

2. C — two
   Tie and two both begin with /t/. Die starts with /d/.

3. D — Choose the meaning that fits your sentence
   Read all meanings and choose the one that matches how the word is used.

4. A — WANJIKU KAMAU, in capital letters only
   Block letters are capital letters.

5. B — Name of the head teacher
   School details include the school name, address and teachers.

6. B — enjoy
   Enjoy has the diphthong /ɔɪ/.

7. B — is written in the text
   Direct answers are stated plainly in the text.

8. C — Why do you think the girl cried?
   The answer must be worked out from clues.

9. C — use clues and think
   Inference means working out the answer from clues.

10. A — There are a lot of children in the yard.
   A lot of is written as three words and is followed by a noun.

11. C — dinner
   Dinner has double n.

12. C — The second
   We say e-MER-gen-cy.

13. C — East
   The sun rises in the east.

14. B — they
   They stands for more than one.

15. B — a farmer
   A noun phrase follows be.

16. C — reading on your own without being told what to read
   You choose and read for yourself.

17. C — biggest
   The last letter doubles: big, bigger, biggest.

18. C — happier
   Change y to i and add er.

19. D — It keeps the ideas in order
   A plan shows what comes first, next and last.

20. B — messages you receive are kept
   The outbox holds messages waiting to be sent.

21. B — a story written from a set of pictures
   The pictures guide the events.

22. B — She was very happy to hear from him.
   Was very happy tells a feeling.

23. B — Kamau bought data bundles yesterday.
   'Bought' and 'yesterday' show the action is finished.

24. A — were
   'They' takes 'were' in the past progressive.

25. B — chicken
   'Chicken' begins with 'ch', said /ʧ/.

26. B — About 60 to 80 words
   The task is a narrative of 60 to 80 words.

27. C — spread
   Germs spread from person to person.

28. D — easy
   The s in 'easy' is buzzed, like z.

29. D — carefully
   'Carefully' tells how something is done.

30. D — hard
   'He works hard' uses hard as an adverb.

31. B — ?
   It is a direct question.

32. C — but
   'But' joins words or sentences.

33. B — The soap gives off a fresh smell.
   'Fresh smell' refers to smell.

34. D — A thumbs-up
   Gestures are nonverbal.

35. B — A netball team has seven players.
   A fact can be checked; the others are opinions.

36. C — Fixing a small problem early prevents a bigger one
   Early action saves later work.

37. B — She has finished.
   Has + past participle.

38. C — The name of the writer of an article
   A byline says who wrote the article.

39. D — opposite
   'The post office is opposite the bank.'

40. D — running
   Double the n.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: We have enough desks to seat every learner. The school has a lot of trees.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pattern and 1 mark for correct punctuation.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: The children put loaves and tomatoes in the boxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for children, loaves and tomatoes and boxes (award 3 for all correct).

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Skimming is reading quickly to get the main idea; scanning is looking quickly for one detail such as a name or number.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: happier, happiest; more beautiful, most beautiful.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: We visited Lake Victoria in August.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for We, 1 mark for Lake Victoria and August, 1 mark for the full stop.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: A: How do we send an email? B: First click Compose. A: Now I type the address. B: Then write your message and press Send.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each line with correct speaker format.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: The coins are in the box. The book is on the table. The cat is under the chair. The shop is between the bank and the school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: /ɛə/: chair, care. /j/: yellow, young. /ʒ/: television.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: as cold as ice, because ice is very cold.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a suitable comparison and 1 mark for the explanation.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Agree on a regular time and a quiet place. Each member reads a book they have chosen. Take turns to tell the group about it and keep a list of the books read.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible sentence.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: The tractor roared like a lion. The day was as hot as a burning coal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable simile.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: written, seen, taken
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: /uː/: food, spoon. /ʊ/: book, cook.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: kite, night. I fly my kite on Saturday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct words and 1 mark for a correct sentence.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: 'Hopping' means jumping, for example 'The rabbit is hopping.' 'Hoping' means wishing, for example 'I am hoping to win.'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for both sentences.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Look at all the pictures, put them in order, ask who, where and what, make notes, think of a title.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, the name of the game, a reason, and a closing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: ship and sheep (or sip); seat and sheet (or sit); sock and shock.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct partner word.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: She is kind and patient. When Cherop pulled up a maize plant by mistake she did not scold but gently explained how to tell weeds from maize.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a trait, 2 marks for the reason.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) I have enough money to buy bread. (b) She has a lot of friends.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: For /v/ the upper teeth touch the lower lip and the voice buzzes; for /w/ the lips are rounded and do not touch the teeth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each description.
